source: due2-native: a party names its policy with odrl:assigneeOf (follow-up review F04, #123)
notes: Valid ODRL 2.2: IM 2.3.3 infers ex:alice as the assignee of every Rule of ex:agreement, and tools/check_odrl22.py applies that inference before validating, so the Agreement has its assignee (IM 2.1.3). due2 does not: W1 reads only the declared edges (odrl-compound-to-atomic-normalization.md §3), so it would see ex:read with no assignee, which permits every requester (due2-workflows.md §5.2), not only ex:alice. The author states the party as odrl:assignee on the Policy or the Rule instead (decisions/0034, amendment of 2026-10-25).

expected_rejection.why: ex:alice names ex:agreement with odrl:assigneeOf, which due2 does not admit; read without the inference, the permission would match any requester. It is a stage-1 error (decisions/0034).
